10.1002_adfm.202517250: Polyethylene oxide (PEO) electrolytes face limitations like low ionic conductivity, poor kinetics, and Li dendrite growth. Within this context, a novel solid‐state electrolyte (SSE) integrates Prussian blue (PB) 3D open framework into a PEO matrix. This design capitalizes on PB uniformly distributed Fe─N≡C sites to establish a bio‐inspired “ion‐selective pumping” effect through dynamic competitive coordination with PEO ether groups (analogous to cellular K + /Na + pumps). The PB framework selectively anchors TFSI − while its electron‐deficient Fe 3+ /Fe 2+ sites promote lithium salt dissociation via Lewis's acid‐base interactions, forcibly stripping Li⁺ from solvation shells into migration pathways. Furthermore, the 3D interconnected nanochannels (15.89 nm) synergize with PEO amorphous regions to create gradient‐pore topological channels. The disorder‐order interfaces at PB‐PEO boundaries induce localized entropy enhancement ( ΔS ↑), thermodynamically driving spontaneous Li + migration through Gibbs free energy minimization. This multi‐scale architecture enables stable Li + deposition/stripping by providing an abundant migration pathway. As a result, Li/PEO@1%PB/Li cells exhibit excellent cycling stability over 2000 h at 0.2 mAh·cm −2 and 6000 h at 0.1 mAh·cm −2 . Li/PEO@1%PB/LFP cells retain 90% capacity after 1000 cycles at 1C. This study offers a new strategy combining ionic coordination and 3D channel design to advance high‐performance all‐solid‐state lithium metal batteries (ASSLMBs).
10.1002_adfm.76296: With the increasing bioanalytical demands, the development of new biodetection techniques is rapidly expanding. Herein, this study reports a new operation mode of energy‐efficient organic photoelectrochemical memtransistor (OPECmT) biodetection. The methodology is synergistically realized by leveraging the characteristics of organic photoelectrochemical transistor (OPECT) and memtransistor. Different from the constantly applied channel voltage ( V D ) in previous OPECT biodetection, only a pulsed V D is needed to operate the OPECmT biodetection without the standby energy input. Significantly, the total energy consumption of OPECmT biodetection is much lower than that of OPECT by two orders of magnitude. Exemplifying by a hybridization chain reaction‐assisted aptasensing, the feasibility of such a technique is then tested by detecting the antibiotic enrofloxacin, which exhibits good analytical performance with a detection limit of 100 ag/mL and lower energy consumption as compared to many published methods. This work features the proof‐of‐concept study of energy‐efficient OPECmT biodetection, which can serve as a generic technique for advanced biological detection.
10.1002_aenm.71717: Ultrathin self‐supporting ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) proton exchange membranes (PEM) are crucial for low‐resistance sustainable energy applications but remain challenging to fabricate. The key to fabricating ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF membranes lies in the compact stacking of iCOF nanosheets, which remains inaccessible through micro‐interfacial polymerization systems. Herein, we report for the first time an ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF PEM constructed by growing few‐layer iCOF nanosheets at high‐curvature micro‐interfaces, alongside a proposed growth mechanism. The curved iCOF exhibits reduced interlayer attraction due to a twisted configuration, and enhanced solvation‐driven exfoliation arising from greater exposure of sulfonic acid groups to water. It avoids the commonly reported nanosphere‐like morphologies in previously reported micro‐interfacial assembly systems by regulating the oil‐in‐water microemulsion interface using weakly surface‐active octanoic acid, which effectively balances between the confined oil phase growth and the unconfined aqueous phase exfoliation. As‐prepared iCOF few‐layer nanosheets (1.3–1.5 nm) expose abundant reactive terminal groups for interlayer crosslinking under the vacuum filtration pressure gradient, leading to ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF PEM (3.2–15.1 µm) with compact layer stacking, good mechanical robustness, and excellent scalability (20 cm in diameter). A fuel cell peak power density of 2017.7 mW cm −2 at 80°C is achieved, surpassing recently reported iCOF‐based membranes.
10.1021_acsami.6c05133: An electrochromic hybrid supercapacitor–battery (EHSB) is developed using a poly(5-cyanoindole)/CoMn 2 O 4 (P5CIn/CMO) composite as the anode and an extended viologen, dipyridyl dibutylpyridine (DPDBPy), embedded in a gel-film matrix as the cathode. The P5CIn/CMO/DPDBPy EHSB operates over a 1.5 V potential window and exhibits reversible deep purple-to-yellow switching via a diffusion-controlled two-electron transfer process, enabled by the extended π-conjugation of the viologen’s central pyridine ring. This leads the EHSB to deliver a coloration efficiency of 153.8 cm 2 C –1, an integrated visible transmission modulation of 50%, and switching times of the order of seconds. Simultaneously, the EHSB delivers an areal specific capacitance (ASC) of 33.3 mF cm –2 (0.3 mA cm –2 ) and a discharge capacity of 89.9 mAh g –1 (0.18 A g –1 ), validating its classification as a hybrid storage device. The cell retains 94% of its ASC over 10,000 cycles in capacitive mode (26.5 mF cm –2 at 1.2 mA cm –2 ), shows a 14.4% decline in diffusive-battery-mode capacity after 100 cycles (80.3 mAh g –1 at 0.3 A g –1 ), and maintains 92% of its optical modulation after 1000 color-switching cycles. The chromatic transition enables real-time visual assessment of the state of charge, positioning the EHSB as a promising platform for scalable integrated energy storage and smart window applications.
